newsitem.title: GERMANY: Berlin may relaunch Bewag privatisation bids.
newsitem.headline: Berlin may relaunch Bewag privatisation bids.

text.p: The Berlin government may relaunch the bidding process to privatise state utility group Berliner Kraft und Licht AG (Bewag) if the remaining foreign bidders pull out of the race.

A spokesman for the Berlin finance ministry said on Tuesday that the government would consider such a step only if all international companies lost interest in the Berlin-based group and said talks with current bidders were still underway.

Industry sources said a consortium of two German bidders, Veba AG and VIAG AG's units PreussenElektra and Bayernwerk, as well as U.S. groups Enron and Southern Company and U.K. group PowerGen were still in the running.
Five other bidders have dropped out since late last year.

The Berlin government on Wednesday said it is very eager to wrap up the negotiations soon as it must sell at least 25.8 percent of the 50.8 percent stake it holds in the utility by the end of February for financial reasons.

The city's finance minister Annette Fugmann-Heesing has said she would favour an international buyer with long-term strategic interests in Bewag and denied reports that any of the remaining foreign bidders had pulled out of the process.
Industry sources said the foreign bidders were unhappy about an existing contract between the city and PreussenElektra and Bayernwerk which would limit their authority.

While a foreign buyer could obtain a majority stake in the Bewag, the group would not receive a majority on Bewag's supervisory board as a contract between Berlin and the two German groups promises them three seats on that board.
A sale to the German bidders could run foul of cartel authorities however as VIAG and Veba already each own a 10 percent stake in Bewag.
